subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the Shahadah, the first of the Five Pillars?
options: The declaration of faith in one God and Muhammad as his prophet
The obligatory almsgiving of surplus wealth
The pilgrimage to the city of Makkah
The fast observed during the month of Ramadan
questions.explain: The Shahadah states 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah'.

questions.q: How many times a day are Muslims required to perform Salah?
options: Three
Five
Seven
Once
questions.explain: Salah is performed five times daily at set times: dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and night.

questions.q: What proportion of a Muslim's surplus wealth is normally given as Zakah each year?
questions.explain: Zakah is the giving of 2.5% of one's savings and surplus wealth to those in need.

questions.q: During which month of the Islamic calendar is Sawm (fasting) observed?
options: Ramadan
Muharram
Shawwal
Dhul-Hijjah
questions.explain: Muslims fast from dawn until sunset throughout the month of Ramadan.

questions.q: Khums, an obligatory act for many Shi'a Muslims, requires the giving of what share of surplus income?
options: One fifth (20%)
One tenth (10%)
One fortieth (2.5%)
One half (50%)
questions.explain: Khums is a 20% tax on surplus income given by Shi'a Muslims, in addition to Zakah.

questions.q: What is the mihrab in a mosque?
options: A niche in the wall showing the direction of Makkah
A raised pulpit used for delivering sermons
A tower from which the call to prayer is made
A basin used for ritual washing
questions.explain: The mihrab is a niche set into the qiblah wall to show worshippers the direction of Makkah.

questions.q: What is the minbar used for in a mosque?
options: It is the raised platform from which the imam delivers the sermon
It is the tower used to call people to prayer
It is the pool used for washing before prayer
It is the dome above the prayer hall
questions.explain: The minbar is a set of steps or pulpit from which the imam gives the khutbah (sermon), especially at Friday prayers.

questions.q: Which festival marks the end of the month of fasting?
options: Id-ul-Fitr
Id-ul-Adha
Ashura
Laylat al-Qadr
questions.explain: Id-ul-Fitr, the 'festival of breaking the fast', celebrates the completion of Ramadan.

questions.q: Why is Hajj significant as one of the Five Pillars?
options: It is a pilgrimage to Makkah that unites Muslims in worship and demonstrates equality before God
It is a daily act of charity given to the poor
It is the weekly congregational prayer held every Friday
It is the recitation of the declaration of faith
questions.explain: Hajj is undertaken at least once by those able, bringing Muslims together at Makkah in a display of unity and equality.

questions.q: Why do Muslims perform wudu before Salah?
options: To achieve ritual purity so they are properly prepared to stand before God
To fulfil the requirement of giving to charity
To signal the beginning of the Friday sermon
To mark the direction they must face in prayer
questions.explain: Wudu is the ritual washing of the hands, face, arms and feet to attain purity before prayer.

questions.q: Why do Muslims face the qiblah when performing Salah?
options: To face the Ka'bah in Makkah, uniting all Muslims in a single direction of worship
To face the sunrise as a sign of new life
To face the minbar where the imam preaches
To face away from images so as not to be distracted
questions.explain: The qiblah is the direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah, which all Muslims turn towards in prayer.

questions.q: Why are there no statues or pictures of God or living beings in a mosque?
options: To avoid idolatry and keep worship focused on God alone
Because decoration is forbidden entirely in Islam
Because such images are too expensive to produce
To leave more room for worshippers to pray
questions.explain: Islam forbids images of God or living creatures to prevent shirk (idolatry) and keep attention on Allah.

questions.q: What is the significance of Jummah for Muslims?
options: It is the Friday congregational prayer that Muslim men are expected to attend at the mosque
It is the fast observed on the tenth day of the month
It is the pilgrimage performed once in a lifetime
It is the private night-time prayer during Ramadan
questions.explain: Jummah is the special midday congregational prayer held on Fridays, including a sermon from the imam.

questions.q: What does Id-ul-Adha commemorate?
options: Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God
The first revelation of the Qur'an to Muhammad
The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala
The completion of the month of fasting
questions.explain: Id-ul-Adha, the 'festival of sacrifice', recalls Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice his son, for whom God provided a ram instead.

questions.q: Why is Ashura especially important for Shi'a Muslims?
options: It commemorates the martyrdom of Husayn, Muhammad's grandson, at Karbala
It celebrates the birth of the Prophet Muhammad
It marks the end of the Hajj pilgrimage
It recalls the migration of Muslims to Madinah
questions.explain: Shi'a Muslims mourn on Ashura in memory of the death of Husayn ibn Ali at the Battle of Karbala.

questions.q: What does Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power) mark?
options: The night the Qur'an was first revealed to Muhammad
The night the Hajj pilgrimage begins
The night marking the birth of Muhammad
The night the fast of Ramadan ends
questions.explain: The Night of Power, observed in the last ten nights of Ramadan, recalls the first revelation of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

questions.q: A Muslim becomes ill during Ramadan and cannot fast. According to Islamic teaching, what is she permitted to do?
options: Make up the missed days of fasting at another time when she is well
Ignore the fast permanently with no further obligation
Perform Hajj instead of fasting that year
Give the Shahadah in place of the missed fasts
questions.explain: Those who are ill are exempt while unwell and are expected to make up the missed fasts later, or pay fidyah if unable.

questions.q: During Hajj, a male pilgrim puts on two plain white unstitched sheets. What does this clothing represent?
options: The state of ihram, showing purity and equality before God
His status as a wealthy pilgrim
That he is leading the Friday prayers
That he has completed the pilgrimage
questions.explain: The white garments of ihram remove distinctions of wealth and status, showing all pilgrims are equal before God.

questions.q: A visitor to a mosque notices worshippers all turning to face a decorated niche in one wall. What is this niche and what does it show?
options: The mihrab, which shows the direction of Makkah
The minbar, from which sermons are given
The minaret, from which prayer is called
The wudu area, used for washing
questions.explain: The mihrab marks the qiblah wall, indicating the direction of Makkah that worshippers face during Salah.

questions.q: Before attending Id-ul-Fitr prayers, a family gives a set amount of money so that the poor can also celebrate the festival. Which practice is this?
options: Zakat-ul-Fitr, charity given before the Id prayer
Khums paid to the imam
The Shahadah recited at Id
Sawm performed on the day of Id
questions.explain: Zakat-ul-Fitr is a charitable donation made before the Id-ul-Fitr prayer so that everyone can share in the celebration.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Religious Studies (J625) specification; Islam: Practices
